title: Patient Financial Account Terms — Late-Fee History and the Good-Faith Percentage
content:
**Term.** The good-faith percentage of a final-notice paydown on the Patient Financial Account is raised by 10 points when the account was charged two or more late fees in the 12 calendar months before the handling date, by 5 points when it was charged exactly one, and by nothing when it was charged none.

| Late fees charged in the 12 calendar months before the handling date | Good-faith percentage raised by |
|---|---|
| 0 | nothing |
| 1 | 5 points |
| 2 | 10 points |
| 3 or more | 10 points |

**Terms explained.**

- A late fee charged is a charge posted on the account ledger with the line category late fee; its posting date decides whether it falls within the 12 months.
- A window of calendar months for the final-notice paydown ends on the handling date and reaches back that many months, a date on the same calendar day that many months earlier falling outside it. A late fee posted on 5 April 2025 is outside the 12 months on a handling date of 5 April 2026 and inside them on 4 April 2026.

**Hypothetical example.** An account charged late fees on 12 November and 12 January, with a handling date of 1 June, was charged two in the 12 months: raised by 10 points. Had the November fee been posted 13 months before the handling date, the count would be one and the percentage raised by 5 points.
